text:
Maxim Shabanov went undrafted, scored 67 points for Traktor Chelyabinsk in the KHL in 2024-25, and got 44 games with the Islanders last season. In Minnesota he has become something else: a power-play finisher. He's on the ice for 72% of the Wild's power-play chances, up from 27%, and nine of his 14 points have come with the extra man.

Our numbers call it a breakout, and the hot run is earned: five goals in his last ten games, with his own chances up too (2.5 expected goals on his shots, against 2.1 usual). Expected goals measure the quality of chances.

The finishing will cool. Nine goals on 5.1 expected means 24% shooting, after 9% last season, and almost nobody holds that. What should last is the role and the chances, now 0.86 expected goals per 60 against 0.62 a year ago. Five-on-five is the soft spot: Minnesota is worse with him on the ice than off it. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a small 8-game sample, had him carrying the puck in on 57% of his entries and exiting cleanly 77% of the time.
headline: Maxim Shabanov found a home on Minnesota's power play
